::: {.tour-notes}
::: {.tour-note-card}
### Start with a bounded group

The existing fixture group makes the three coded records visible so the operator can verify what would be in scope before a live run.
:::

::: {.tour-note-card}
### Pause at each decision

The tour pauses at the staged rubric request, stored rubric, deterministic mapping, fixture result inspection, and human review instead of implying that every detail occupies one screen.
:::

::: {.tour-note-card}
### End with human review

Review controls remain explicit. The final screen stops before saving so the tour demonstrates the decision surface without mutating even the synthetic fixture.
:::
:::

::: {.tour-method}
## What this tour represents

These screens use the production MAPLES React interface from OASIS commit 90031150529bbfa1a3de4f5769039fb91940ed08 against a deterministic same-origin loopback fixture. The live MAPLES stack and grading pipeline were not used. Provider calls, external service clients, outbound connections, and spend were all zero. Displayed scores, rationales, progress, and review states are authored fixture values—not model outputs.

The published page replays seven static WebP screenshots. Visitors do not connect to MAPLES or call its APIs. The public media manifest records the source revision, fixture boundary, hashes, dimensions, zero-provider evidence, and privacy review.

The Perfume Making → Candle Making narrative was inspired by Minhan Park and Licheng Yi’s [public walkthrough](https://ut-real-ai-project-maples.com/wayfinder-rubric-authoring-demo) and [video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MKwseFKuFLs). All rubric wording, notes, scores, rationales, and coded records in this tour were newly authored. This is not a reproduction of the interns’ original prompts, outputs, data, runtime, or exact demo.

**Wayfinder Rubric Studio** helps create or upload rubric material inside the MAPLES web workflow. **Wayfinder Operator** is the distinct CLI/TUI experience. They share an ecosystem name and related goals, but they are sibling profiles with different interfaces and trust boundaries.

<details class="tour-transcript">
<summary>Read the seven-step walkthrough</summary>

1. **Group:** Open the existing Candle Making group and verify that it contains only DEMO-001, DEMO-002, and DEMO-003.
2. **Rubric path:** Stage the reconstructed Perfume-to-Candle request in Create Rubric. The request is not submitted, so no Wayfinder or provider call occurs.
3. **Inspect rubric:** Open the stored synthetic rubric and inspect its ready version, Note modality, three criteria, questions, and controls indicating four scoring levels.
4. **Configure:** Match Candle Making and Scented Container Candle to the Candle Making Station. The suggestion shown is deterministic fixture data.
5. **Run states:** Compare seeded Running and Completed interface states and their visible progress. The capture does not start a grading pipeline.
6. **Results:** Select DEMO-001 and inspect its synthetic source note, recorded fixture score, and deterministic assessment and rationale.
7. **Review:** Choose reviewed score 3 and add a synthetic comment. The screenshot is taken before Save Review, so no review mutation occurs.

</details>
:::
